(a) innovation capacity development was positively associated with exposure to theoretical innovation curricula and (b) innovation capacity development occurred for students who were exposed to theoretical innovation curricular learning experiences.

students who participated in the innovation course or the single-session innovation experience reported significant gains in innovation capacities, whereas students not exposed to innovation curricula did not.
exposure to innovation curricula is positively related to the development of innovation capacities, but the effect is small.

the development of innovation capacities in undergraduates.
the development of undergraduate students’ capacities to engage in the innovation process.

the question of whether and to what extent undergraduate students’ exposure and participation in a theoretically designed innovation learning experience can promote innovation capacities, a measurable set of selfperceptions and abilities students develop to better engage innovation.

this study suggests that innovation capacity development is associated with exposure to theoretical designed innovation curriculum.

the results of this study support the value of curricular approaches to developing students’ innovation capacities.

innovation capacities are malleable and that curricula can play an important role in developing them.
